object_description: a free-standing solitary hall and an elongated, staggered residential building connected underground
design_condition: the hall stands free in the middle of a public square that flows around the volumes, with the elongated residential building along the lane and the ancillary uses buried between them

positive: The site is conceived as a public square that flows freely around the volumes with differently designed zones
Lowering the inner courtyard with seating steps is a promising approach for the hall entrance
The seating arena offers additional usage potential for the outdoor space in combination with the hall
The hall is clearly recognisable as a public building through its placement in the middle of the square
The special use is reflected in the expressive form and a decided architectural expression of high recognition value
The solitaire impresses with its compact overall form and projecting canopies on two sides
An interesting polygonal event space with a well-proportioned foyer and functional side extensions is proposed
The slender, height-graduated residential building has a delicate appearance and blends in well with the surroundings
The daytime cafe is convincing as an appropriate, neighbourhood-compatible use with activation potential for the square
The apartments are well laid out in their two-sided orientation, bright and user-friendly
A very self-confident and interesting urban planning approach, with square and solitaire carefully designed
negative: Inserting the hall volume into the courtyard leads to cramped situations in the spaces between the buildings
The purely mineral courtyard design and the theatrical staging ignore the need for green recreational space
No statements are made on how to deal with the existing basement uses
The chosen stage shape is formalistic, difficult to use and acoustically questionable
The passages from stage to backstage and instrument room are too narrow and the backstage is significantly lower than the stage
Delivery via a lift is inconvenient and unsuitable in the proposed size
There are no checkrooms for visitors and food can only be delivered through the storage room
Most functional deficiencies stem from the basement location and are therefore of a fundamental nature
Ground floor therapy rooms facing the square should be questioned because of the views
The location of the two house entrances appears random and contributes little to address formation
The apartment formulation is schematic, with no precise statements on structural design and facade effect
The living space per apartment is very large and correspondingly expensive, so the apartments are not in line with the market
Realisation requires increased coordination due to the overlapping uses, presumably by different sponsors
